title: DentiMax Summit Spotlights Workflow
html:
By News Staff

November 16, 2026

Share

Dental technology should make the practice day easier, not add another dashboard, DentiMax executives said at the company’s 2026 Dental Tech Summit, held Nov. 5-6 in Mesa. The event also featured sessions on patient communication, artificial intelligence (AI), and the leadership and training involved in adopting new systems.

DentiMax previewed updates to its cloud-based practice management software, DentiMax Flow, including AI voice charting, voice-activated periodontal charting, and AI voice clinical notes. The company said the periodontal feature is designed to let clinicians record measurements while keeping their attention on the patient and clinical workflow. Other updates presented included online payments, automated patient communications, Mango Voice integration, and patient kiosk uploads for insurance and identification cards.

The Summit also marked the official naming of DentiMax Frame, imaging software previously introduced in beta and refined with feedback from participating dental offices. Chad Camac and Travis Fleming showcased the company’s digital sensor lineup, including the DentiMax Pro, highlighting image quality, reliability, and options for different practice needs, workflows, and budgets.

“Nobody at a front desk wakes up wanting another dashboard. They want the day to run a little smoother, and that’s what we kept hearing in the room,” said Alicia Dieujuste, managing director of DentiMax Software.

Sessions emphasized that technology’s usefulness depends on how it fits into practice operations and patient interactions. Sherrie Busby, EDDA, CDSO, a dental assistant training developer and speaker, opened the Summit with a keynote on how preparation, empathy, trust, and team alignment can shape the patient experience before treatment. On the second day, Tyler Fessler of Mango Voice discussed the phone as another early patient touchpoint and how communication tools can help practices avoid losing patient connections.

Amy Manzo, a dental operations and leadership expert, addressed technology adoption. She urged practices to explain why a process is changing before teaching staff how to use a system, understand resistance, map workflows before digitizing them, and plan for repeated training. “Technology is the tool. Leadership makes the change stick,” Manzo said.

AI sessions focused on current operational uses. Hamed Fesharaki, BDS, co-founder and chief executive officer of Adravision, discussed surfacing information from radiographs, charts, treatment plans, and claims for dentists to review. Heidi Brannon of DentalXChange presented Eligibility AI, which is designed to check coverage before visits and bring benefits information from different payers into a more consistent view.

DentiMax President and Co-Founder David Arnett said the goal was for technology to improve practice operations without becoming a distraction. 

“The best technology is the kind you stop noticing. The practice just runs better, and the team gets its day back,” he said.
